translations.text: Lamentation came there, and the idols fell. The day was glorious over the earth when the multitude set out.
(Their lands were covered with a helmet of cloud), border-dwellings on the moorland slopes. Moses led the army over them, past many dangers [?].
They were forced into narrow northern paths. They knew that to the south of them lay the land of the Ethiopians, hill-slopes scorched, a people browned by the hot coals of heaven.
There holy God shielded the people against the sudden burning. He spread a canopy over the burning sky, a holy net over the hot air.
A heavenly beacon rose every evening, another wonder. After the sun had gone down its setting-course, it was seen, strangely, shining with flame over the people: a burning pillar.
Clear beams stood bright over the warriors. The shields shone and the shadows vanished. The deep shadows of night could not hide their hiding-places nearby. The candle of heaven burned.
The camp was set up. The weary men refreshed themselves. The brave servers brought food to them, and they restored their strength.

There sudden news came into their army, terror from inland. Fear arose, the dread of slaughter among the hosts. The exile awaited the hateful pursuer, who long before had imposed hardship on them, the homeless ones, and bound them in woe with torments.
They did not heed the covenant, though the elder king had once become guardian [?] of the native peoples, of men, in return for treasures [?], so that he prospered so greatly [?].
They forgot all this after the race of the Egyptians grew angry over a dispute [?]. Then they committed murder against his kinsmen, contrived accusations, and broke the covenant.

The surges of hostility lay close to their hearts, the passion of the men. With wicked faithlessness they meant to repay that reward for life with treachery, so that the people of Moses should pay for that day's work with blood, where mighty God had granted them success on that journey of destruction.

Then the courage of the men turned to despair once they saw Pharaoh's army coming on from the southern ways, carrying their forest of spears, the troop glittering (spears were arrayed, the battle moved on,
At times proud thanes from that host measured out the miles on horseback.

The war-leader of men fastened his grim helmet, the king his chin-guard (banners glittered), expecting battle. He shook his coat of mail and ordered his chosen troop to hold the battle formation firmly. With hostile eyes the friends [?] watched the coming of the people of the land.
Therefore each one led out every warrior of the male sex that he could find in that time.
The fugitives had the space of a night, though enemies lurked on every side of them, an army on one side and the sea on the other. They had no other way out.
They had lost hope of their rightful homeland. They sat along the hills in shining [?] garments, expecting woe. The whole band of kinsmen waited together, keeping watch, for the greater force,

until Moses ordered the men at dawn, with brazen trumpets, to gather the people: the warriors were to rise, take up their coats of mail, set their minds on courage, carry their bright armour, and call the troop with signals nearer to the sand.

those who because of their youth could not yet, under the cover of shields, defend the mail-shirts of men against the treacherous foe with their hands, and had not yet suffered a deadly wound over the rim of a shield, a grievous bodily wound, in the boastful play of the spear.
This is the eternal God of Abraham, Lord of creation, who protects this army, brave and mighty, with his great hand."
They did not take to heart the teaching of the holy one at all, after the song of the beloved one [?] nearer the end [?], when the sound and the mingled singing died away.

Then the fourth tribe went first and waded into the waves, warriors in a band, over the green sea-floor. The troop of Judah, alone in the vanguard [?], went onto the unknown path ahead of its kinsmen.
After that army the seafarers grew bold, the sons of Reuben. The sea-warriors carried their shields over the salt marsh, a multitude of men. A great single troop went on unafraid.

After them came the sons of Simeon, marching on in their tribes and companies. The third great nation pressed forward as a picked war-band, dewy with spear-shafts, while banners waved above the advancing spears.

Each man knew the law of the kindreds and the noble descent of his people, as Moses had told them. They had one father, a beloved founder of the nation, wise in spirit and dear to his kinsmen, who had received the right to the land.
Noah, the glorious prince, sailed with his three sons over new floods: the deepest of the drowning floods that ever came about in the kingdom of the world.
So wise men say in their words that Abraham's father was the ninth from Noah in the count of the generations.
Afterwards, at the command of the Holy One, he led the one whose life was dearest to him. The kinsmen climbed the high land, up onto the mountain of Zion.
Abraham led his son Isaac to that meeting place. The fire of the pyre was kindled. The first slayer of life was none the gladder for it.

Heaven and earth cannot encompass the word of his glory. It is wider and broader than the corners of the earth can embrace, wider than the circle of the world and the heavens above, the expanse of the ocean and this sad air.
The mountain slopes were drenched with blood, and the sea spewed out gore. There was an outcry on the waves. The water was full of weapons, and a mist of death rose up.

The proud nations could not hold back the path of the helpers [?] or the fury of the sea-current. With its screaming terror it struck down many. The ocean raged; it rose up, then slid down. Terrors stood, and the death-wounds welled.

The flood-pale army, held fast all around, gave up their souls [?] after the dark surge came down on them, the greatest of the raging waves. The whole host perished when the Egyptian force was drowned, Pharaoh together with his peoples.
Then, on the shore of the sea, Moses, the man of high excellence, spoke eternal counsels to the Israelites: holy speech, a profound message.
He shines more light on us now that scholars tell us better of the longer joys of life. This joy here is fleeting. It is cursed with sins, granted to exiles, a time of waiting for the wretched.
"Great is this multitude. Strong is the leader of hosts, the greatest of helpers, who leads this journey. Among the race of Canaan he has granted us cities and rings of treasure and a broad kingdom.

Now the Lord of angels intends to fulfil what he long ago promised with an oath to the race of your fathers in days of old. If you keep the holy teaching, you will go on to overcome every one of your enemies. You will possess a victorious kingdom between the seas, the beer-halls of men. Great will be your glory!"

After those words the host was joyful. The trumpets of victory sang with a fair sound, and the banners stood raised. The people were on land. The beam of glory had led the host, the holy companies, into God's keeping [?].
They rejoiced in their lives, now that they had brought them out of the power of their enemies. They had dared it boldly, these men beneath the roofs of the waters.
They saw the walls standing there. All the seas through which they had carried their war-gear seemed bloody to them.
Then it was easy to find African women on the shore of the ocean, adorned with gold.
